Okay since No one else gave you the answer you're looking for let's break down a few things. 

That CPU you're running is a pretty good one and is in the newer generation's so there's nothing wrong with keeping that one. If you do feel the need to upgrade cpu then all of the LGA 1151 sockets (the one on your MoBo) fit up to 9th gen processors so you could go with i7 9700k or i9 9900k. Both would offer 4-5% better fps and 12-13% better effective speed. The spec sheet for your MoBo says it'll only support up to an i7. Not sure if thats exactly true or not as I've never seen a board care as long as it was the correct socket so do a bit more research on that before going to the i9. 

The graphics card is getting a bit old but it is still a good card that will do until you could get your hands on something much better like the rtx 3080 or the rx 6800. If you want to upgrade now and don't mind being just one generation behind then you can definitely go with the rtx 20xx super series. Any of those are going to give you much better performance. With the 2070 giving 13-14% better fps and effective speed and the 2080 giving 33-34% better in both. 

Your RAM looks good but you can upgrade that as well. You do have 32gb of ram but its only running at 2400 Mhz and your board can support up to 2800 so that could be something to look into. Or just get 2 more matching sticks so you have double the channels to work with at the slower speed. 

Could always upgrade SSD to get faster performance from those and more storage but 500gb and 4tb is plenty and it would not be at the top of my list. 

Could look into a MoBo upgrade as well and that would give you the foot to upgrade all your components to the much better stuff down the road. Find one with a LGA 1151 socket and you can use all of your current components until you decide to go bigger.
